source.title: Interpreting Adversarial Examples by Activation Promotion and Suppression
source.authors: Kaidi Xu; Si-Jia Liu; Gaoyuan Zhang; Meng-Shu Sun; Pu Zhao; Quan-Fu Fan; Chuang Gan; X. Lin

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies semantic interpretability of selected CNN units under adversarial attacks, but it does not test any listed version: it neither audits the proportion of neurons with one or two jobs nor tests the listed language-model, polysemantic-neuron, circuit, or explanation-scoring claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports network-dissection measurements relevant to unit interpretability; these findings are recorded under fits_no_version because they do not measure any listed version. The neuron-masking robustness results and the pixel- and image-level attack results do not measure the listed claims and are not rows. Cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The paper uses network dissection (Bau et al. 2017) as a tool to label ResNet-152 units with concepts and relates adversarial sensitivity to that interpretability. It reports no share of neurons with one main job across a whole model, no polysemanticity analysis, no circuit or attribution-graph test, and no held-out scoring of explanations, so none of V1–V7 is tested. T4 fits better than T6, because network-dissection unit interpretability is used as an instrument rather than merely cited.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors' main conclusions are about adversarial perturbations: a promotion-suppression effect at pixel level, links to CAM discriminative regions, and a link between unit sensitivity and network-dissection concept interpretability. Neuron masking is offered as a preliminary robustness insight, raising adversarial accuracy at a slight cost in clean accuracy. The record's paraphrase omits the pixel-level and CAM conclusions, but what it states is accurate.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses network dissection and adversarial-sensitivity measurements on a vision CNN, not an audit of neuron-pole explanations tested on held-out activating examples.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported sensitivity–interpretability association varies with layer depth and with the number N of top sensitive units considered.

fits_no_version.finding: In ResNet-152 on Broden, the units most sensitive to PGD perturbations have higher network-dissection IoU than randomly chosen units (p<0.05 in most cases). The link is stronger in deeper layers (conv4_36, conv5_3) and grows with N up to 100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Units that are sensitive to adversarial perturbations in vision CNNs tend to be concept-interpretable under network dissection, especially in deep layers.

record.problems: The interpretability analysis concerns selected adversarially sensitive units, not all units, and is limited to Resnet 152 and Broden. The paper reports only an aggregate textual summary of the p-values; exact values and concept-detector counts are in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Pixel-level perturbation sensitivity, CAM interpretability, and attack-refinement results in Sections 3–4 and Appendix Table A1 do not measure the listed neuron-interpretability claims. Appendix Table A2 measures adversarial robustness after neuron masking, not whether neurons have one main job or suffice as circuit units.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B audit and no neuron-pole job shares.
No language models or scale comparison.
No comparison of architectures, regularization or tools on the interpretable-neuron share.
No neuron-based circuits or attribution graphs.
No test of whether explanations predict activations beyond the activating examples.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from 'discusses'/T6 to 'uses_without_test'/T4, because network dissection is used as a tool. The paper's notion of unit interpretability uses a lenient threshold (max IoU>0.04), averages IoU over concepts, and covers only selected units, so it cannot inform the V1/V4 share estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit, neuron-pole job counts, or estimate of one-job, two-related-job, and not-understood shares.
No language models, model-scale sweep, dense-versus-MoE comparison, or estimates up to trillions of parameters.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or test of pose, recursive generalization, or superposition.
No comparison of architectures, regularization, or explanation tools for the share of interpretable neurons.
No attribution graphs or test of whether a model's own neurons explain behavior without a replacement model.
No test of explanations against activations on examples different from those used to write the explanations.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by predicting activations on new text.

rows.subject: Resnet 152
rows.operation_detail: Compared network-dissection interpretability of the top N units ranked by sensitivity to PGD adversarial perturbations against a background distribution from randomly selected units.
rows.measure: p-value for interpretability of the top N sensitive units against the random-unit IoU distribution
rows.baseline: IoU distribution when N units are randomly picked
rows.uncertainty: p-values are the reported significance measure; exact values are figure-only
rows.note: The paper reports the aggregate qualitative result in text; the figure plots separate values by layer and N, but exact values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: The measure is a p-value for the IoU of the top-N adversarially sensitive units against randomly picked units. It is a sensitivity–interpretability association on selected units, not a share of interpretable neurons. The 'observed' state refers only to the paper's own association, which is fine as a fits_no_version finding.

rows.subject: Resnet 152
rows.operation_detail: Compared the sensitivity–interpretability association across shallow and deep layers.

conditions.value: shallow: conv2_3 and conv3_8; deep: conv4_36 and conv5_3
top N sensitive units, with N in {10, 20, 30, 50, 80, 100}

rows.measure: Strength of the connection between unit sensitivity to adversarial perturbations and network-dissection interpretability
rows.value: The connection is stronger in conv4_36 and conv5_3 than in conv2_3 and conv3_8.
rows.note: The authors attribute the weaker shallow-layer result to subtle activation changes that are less detectable by interpretability.
rows.check: This is a layer comparison of the same sensitivity–interpretability association. It does not measure any version's construct.

rows.subject: Resnet 152
rows.operation_detail: Compared the sensitivity–interpretability association as the number of top sensitive units N increased within a layer.
rows.measure: Significance of interpretability among the top N units ranked by adversarial sensitivity
rows.baseline: Smaller N within the same layer
rows.value: The connection becomes more significant as N increases.
rows.uncertainty: p-values are the reported significance measure; exact values are figure-only
rows.note: The authors state that most of the top 100 sensitive units are interpretable, while the top 10 sensitive units might not be the same as the top 10 interpretable units.
rows.check: The trend across N concerns selected sensitive units. The phrase 'most of top 100 sensitive units are interpretable' is qualitative and covers selected units only, not a model-wide share.

rows.subject: Resnet 152

conditions.value: color, texture, material, part, object, scene

rows.measure: Number of concept detectors by category among the top 100 sensitive units
rows.value: Figure only; text says low-level concepts such as color and texture dominate at lower layers, while more high-level concepts such as object and part emerge in deeper layers.
rows.note: The plot reports counts by layer and category, but exact counts are not stated in the text.
rows.check: The values are figure-only counts of concept detectors among the top-100 sensitive units, using the network-dissection IoU>0.04 threshold. They are not a share of all units and give no one-job versus multi-job split.

relation.reason: Applies network dissection unit labels without testing whether neurons are already interpretable.

tranche.reason: Uses network dissection as a tool and reports its own sensitivity-interpretability association; reports no model-wide share of one-job neurons and does not test any version.

source_check.notes: Exact p-values and detector counts are figure-only. Results concern selected adversarially sensitive units in ResNet-152 (IoU averaged over concepts), not the share of neurons with one job.

statements.correction: Text: ResNet-152, PGD untargeted adversarial examples from Broden; IoU of top-N sensitive units vs random-unit IoU distribution gives p < 0.05 in most cases; deep layers conv4_36 and conv5_3 show a stronger connection than conv2_3 and conv3_8 (Section 5, Figure 9(a)).
